questions.q: Consider a spongy block of mass $m$ floating on a flowing river. The maximum mass of the block is related to the speed of the river flow $v$, acceleration due to gravity $g$ and the density of the block $\rho$ such that $m_{\max }=k v^x g^y \rho^z(k$ is constant $)$. The values of $x, y$ and $z$ should then respectively be (Mass of the spongy block is assumed to vary due to absorption of water by it)
questions.solution: Since, the maximum mass of the block floating on river depends, speed of flow of the river $=v$, acceleration due to gravity $=g$ and density of the block $=\rho$, $m_{\max }=k v^x g^y \rho^z$ Compairing the dimensions of $\mathrm{M}, \mathrm{L}$ and $\mathrm{T}$ on both sides, we get $z=1\begin{aligned} x+y-3 z & =0 \\ -x-2 y & =0 \\ x+y-3 \times 1 & =0[\text { [From Eq. (i) and (ii)] } \\ x+y & =3\end{aligned}$ From Eqs. (iii) and (iv), we get $-y=3 \Rightarrow y=-3$ From Eq. (iv), we have $\begin{aligned} & & x-3 & =3 \\ \Rightarrow & & x & =6\end{aligned}$ Hence, the value of $x, y$ and $z$ will be $(6,-3,1)$.

questions.q: If the energy, $E=G^p h^q c^r$, where $G$ is the universal gravitational constant, $h$ is the Planck's constant and $c$ is the velocity of light, then the values of $p, q$ and $r$ are, respectively
questions.solution:
$E=G^p h^q c^r\begin{aligned}$& {\left[\mathrm{M}^1 $\mathrm{~L}^2 $\mathrm{~T}^{-2}\right]=\left[\mathrmM^{-1} \mathrm{~L}^3 $\mathrm{~T}^{-2}\right]^p\left[\mathrm{ML}^2 $\mathrm{~T}^{-1}\right]^q\left[\mathrm{LT}^{-1}\right]^r} \\
& =\mathrmM^{-p+q} $\mathrm{~L}^{3 p+2 q+r} \mathrm{~T}^{-2 p-q-r}
\end{aligned}$Applying principle of homogeneity of dimensions, we get $\begin{aligned}$& -p+q=1 \\
& 3 p+2 q+r=2 \\
& -2 p-q-r=-2
\end{aligned} Add (iii) and (iv), $p+q=0$
Add (ii) and (v), we get $q=\frac{1}{2}$
From (ii), we get $p=q-1=\frac{1}{2}-1=-\frac{1}{2}$.
Put in (iii), we get $-\frac{3}{2}+1+r=2, \quad r=5 / 2$

questions.q: Assertion (A) Energy per unit volume and angular momentum can be added dimensionally. Reason (R) Physical quantities having same dimensions can be added or subtracted.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution: The units of energy per unit volume is $\mathrm{J} / \mathrm{m}^3$ or $\mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{m}-\mathrm{s}^2$ and that for angular momentum is $\mathrm{kg}-\mathrm{m}^2 / \mathrm{s}$. Since, they are not dimensionally equal, they cannot be added, so the Assertion (A) is false. Only those physical quantities that have same dimensions can be added or subtracted, so Reason (R) is true. Hence, the correct option is $(\mathrm{d})$.

questions.solution:
Let $Y = f \left(V, F, a\right)$

$∴ Y = {KV}^{x}F^{y}a^{z}, K \to$Unitless

$∴ \left[Y\right] = \left[V\$right]x\left[$F\right]y\left[a\right]z$

$∴ \left[{ML}^{- 1}T^{- 2}\right] = \left[{LT}^{- 1}\rright]x\left[{MLT}^{- 2}\rright]y\left[{LT}^{- 2}\right]z$

$∴ \left[M\$right]\left[$L^{- 1}\right] = \left[$T^{- 2}\right]{=}^{} \left[M\right]y\left[L^{x + y + z}\right]\left[T^{- x - 2y - 2z}\right]$

$∴ y = 1; x + y + z = - 1; - x - 2y - 2z = 2$

$∴ x + z = - 2 ∴ x + 2y + 2z = 2$

$∴ x + 2z = 0∴ z = 2, x = - 4$

$∴ \left[Y\right] = \left[$V^{- 4}{Fa}^{2}\right]$

questions.q: The speed of ripples $( v )$ on water surface depends on surface tension $( \sigma )$, density $( ρ )$, and wavelength $( \lambda )$. Then the square of speed $( v )$ is proportional to
questions.solution:
Speed of ripples,& $v$~depends on~$\sigma, ρ, \lambda$

$⇒ v ∝ {σ}^{a}{ρ}^{b}{λ}^{c}$

$⇒ \left[M^{0}LT^{- 1}\right] ∝ \left[MT^{- 2}\right]a\left[ML^{- 3}\right]b\left[L\right]c$

$⇒ \left[M^{0}LT^{- 1}\right] ∝ \left[M\right]a + b\left[L\right]- 3b + c\left[T\right]- 2a$

By equating the powers,~$⇒ a + b = 0, - 3b + c = 1, - 2a = - 1$

$⇒ a = \dfrac{1}{2}, b = - \dfrac{1}{2}, c = - \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ v ∝ \sigma\dfrac{1}{2}{ρ}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}}{λ}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}}$

$⇒ v ∝ \sqrt{\dfrac{σ}{ρ\lambda}} ⇒ v^{2} ∝ \dfrac{σ}{ρ\lambda}$

questions.q: The expressions below give current $I$ through an electronic component as a function of applied potential $V . I_0$ and $V_0$ are constants having dimensions of current and potential respectively. Which of the following are dimensionally incorrect? (A) $I=I_0 $\$left(e^{\frac{2 V}{V_0}}+$1\right)$ (B) $I=I_0  \left(e^{\frac{v}{2 V_0}}-1\right)$ (C) $I=I_0 V_0 $\$left(e^{\frac{V}{V_0}}-$1\right)$ (D) $I=I_0\$left(\frac{V}{V_0}\right) \left(e^{\frac{V}{V_0}}-1\right)$
questions.solution: According to the principle of homogeneity, a physical equation will be dimensionally correct only if the dimensions of all the terms occuring on both side of the equation are the same. Hence, in option (c) I=I_0 V_0\left($e^{\frac{v}{V_0}}-1\right) Dimension of $I \neq$ dimensions of $I_0 V_0$ Therefore, equation shown in option (c) is not dimensionally correct.$

questions.q: Number of particles, given by $n = - D\dfrac{{n}_{2} - {n}_{1}}{{x}_{2} - {x}_{1}}$, is crossing a unit area perpendicular to $x$-axis in unit time, where ${n}_{1}$ and ${n}_{2}$ are number of particles per unit volume for the value of $x$ meant to ${x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{1}$ . Find dimensions of $D$, called as diffusion constant.
questions.solution:
Given, number of particle passing from unit area in unit time $= n$

$= \dfrac{Numberofparticle}{A \times t} = \dfrac{ \left[M^{0}L^{0}T^{0}\right]}{ \left[$L^{2}\right]\left[T\right]} = \left[L^{- 2}T^{- 1}\right]$

\left[{n}_{1}\right] = \left[{n}_{2}\right] =Numberofparticleinunitvolume = \left[L^{- 3}\right]$

Now, from the given formula \left[$D\right] = $\dfrac{\left[n\right]\left[{x}_{2} - {x}_{1}\right]}{ \left[{n}_{2} - {n}_{1}\right]}

$= $\dfrac{ \left[L^{- 2}T^{- 1}\right] \left[$L\right]}${ \left[$L^{- 3}\right]}$

$= \left[$L^{2}T^{- 1}\right]

questions.q: If dimensions of critical velocity, ${v}_{c}$ of a liquid flowing through a tube are expressed as  \left[{η}^{x}{ρ}^{y}r^{z}\right]$, where, $η, ρ$ and $r$ are the coefficient of viscosity of liquid, density of liquid and radius of the tube, respectively, then, the values of $x$, $y$ and $\text{z}$ are given by$
questions.solution:
Dimensions of velocity, coefficient of viscosity and density are,

\left[v\right] = \left[{LT}^{- 1}\right]

\left[η\right] = \left[F\right]\lleft[A\dfrac{d v}{d x}\right] = \left[{MLT}^{- 2}\right] \left[L^{2}\right]\left[$T^{- 1}\right] = \left[{ML}^{- 1}T^{- 1}\right]$

\left[$ρ\right] = \left[{ML}^{- 3}\right]$

Now, \left[v\right] = \left[η\$right]x\left[$ρ\$right]y \left[$r\right]z$

$⇒ \left[{LT}^{- 1}\right] = \left[{ML}^{- 1}$T^{- 1}\$right]x\left[{ML}^{- 3}\right]$y \left[L\right]z$

Now, by using dimensional homogeneity, we will get,

$M^{0} = M\left(x + y\right)$

$⇒ y = - x$

For $T$,

$x = 1$

$⇒ y =- x =- 1$

For $L$,

$1 = - x - 3y + z$

$⇒ z = - 1$

$

Velocity of surface waves depends on density of water, its own wavelength of surface tension.

$v ∝ {ρ}^{a}{\lambda}^{b}{\gamma}^{c}$

\left[LT^{- 1}\right] ∝ {\left[ML^{- 3}\right]}^{a}{\left[L\right]}^{b}{\left[\dfrac{MLT^{- 2}}{L}\right]}^{c}$

\left[LT^{- 1}\right] ∝ M^{a + c}L^{- 3a + b}T^{- 2c}$

$a + c = 0 ..........(i)$

$- 3a + b = 1 .............(ii)$

$- 2c = - 1 .............(iii)$

Solving
$a = - \dfrac{1}{2}, b = - \dfrac{1}{2}, c = \dfrac{1}{2 ,}$

$v ∝ {ρ}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}}{\lambda}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}}{\gamma}^{\dfrac{1}{2}}$

$v ∝ \sqrt{\dfrac{\gamma}{ρ\lambda}}$
